title: On the Reliability of User-Centric Evaluation of Conversational Recommender Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Using crossed random-effects models and variance-based metrics like the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) to isolate systematic annotator-specific scale effects (i.e., personal bias such as consistent strictness or leniency) from actual dialogue quality variance.

Computing pairwise Spearman correlations and applying hierarchical clustering to user-centric evaluation dimensions to determine if human evaluators conflate distinct metrics (like accuracy, satisfaction, and usability) into a single overall impression of quality.
